hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $\overline{CG}$

Under this transformation, some points on the parallelogram map to another point which is no longer on the parallelogram.  


[[☃ image 1]]

The parallelogram is *not symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A pre-image parallelogram with vertices at A, C ,G and E. Side A G has a midpoint H. Side C E has a midpoint D. Both sides A G and C E are congruent. Side A C has a midpoint B. Side G E has a midpoint F. Both sides A C and G E are congruent. A blue line connects from vertex C to vertex G on the other side of the parallelogram. The outline of the image parallelogram is reflected across segment C G with vertices E and A not touching the pre-image parallelogram.

##Reflection over $\overline{DH}$

Under this transformation, some points on the parallelogram map to another point which is no longer on the parallelogram.  


[[☃ image 1]]

The parallelogram is *not symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A pre-image parallelogram with vertices at A, C ,G and E. Side A G has a midpoint H. Side C E has a midpoint D. Both sides A G and C E are congruent. Side A C has a midpoint B. Side G E has a midpoint F. Both sides A C and G E are congruent. A blue line connects from midpoint D to midpoint H on the other side of the parallelogram. The outline of the image parallelogram is reflected across segment D H with vertices C and G not touching the pre-image parallelogram.

hints.content:
Neither symmetry applies to the parallelogram.

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{CG}$ | No
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{DH}$ | No
